plan.line: a small 0.96 inch 128x64 OLED display (I2C, SSD1306). Use it only when the idea names a 0.96 inch display or an SSD1306; otherwise the 1.3 inch OLED. At most 2 displays.

code.pinLine:
0.96" OLED display {ref} on I2C{bus} (SDA {gpio}, SCL {scl}): set it up with i2c{n} = I2C({bus}, sda=Pin({g}), scl=Pin({sclG}), freq=400000) and oled{n} = SSD1306_I2C(128, 64, i2c{n}). Draw with oled{n}.fill(0) (clear), oled{n}.text("Hi", x, y), oled{n}.rect/line/pixel, then call oled{n}.show() once after drawing. Not sh1106: this display is SSD1306.
  This screen: letters are 8x8 pixels, so 8 text rows at y = 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56 (the last row is y = 56) and at most 16 characters per row. The built-in font has only plain ASCII characters.
  Drawing helpers in ssd1306.py (use them: numbers, levels and pictures look much better than plain text): oled{n}.title("Weather") draws a lit bar at the top (draw the rest from y = 12); oled{n}.center_text("Ready", y) centres text; oled{n}.center_text("4:59", y, scale=3, style="seg") and oled{n}.big_text("23", x, y, scale=2, style="block") draw big text. Text styles: {TEXT_STYLES} (block = the font enlarged, dots = LED-matrix look from scale 3, seg = clock-like digits). Every style is 8 x scale pixels wide per character (scale 2: at most 8 characters per row, scale 3: 5); block and dots are 8 x scale tall, seg 11 x scale tall. oled{n}.bar(x, y, w, h, value, max_value, style="solid") draws a level or progress bar; bar styles: {BAR_STYLES}. oled{n}.graph(readings, x, y, w, h, low, high) draws a line graph of a list of numbers (keep the last readings in a list). oled{n}.icon("heart", x, y, scale=2) draws an 8x8 icon (scale 2 = 16x16); icons: {ICONS}. oled{n}.sprite(["..##..", ".####.", "######"], x, y, scale=2) draws your own small picture, one text row per pixel row, "#" lit and "." dark: use it for anything the icons don't have.
code.moduleRule: ssd1306 when a 0.96" OLED display is listed
